title: ADR 0003: probe the REAL bd metadata ceiling on the production path
description: Phase-0 probe 2 used --metadata=@file.json (scratchpad/probes/phase0-results.md:19-23). Production passes canonical JSON inline as ONE argv element (bdio/client.py:334-335). Linux MAX_ARG_STRLEN = 32 x 4096 = 131072 bytes. So the probe validated a path production never takes and the real ceiling is likely ~128KiB, kernel-imposed. (1) Sweep/binary-search serialized sizes around failure using a real RootMetadata; multibyte UTF-8; create, self-ID merge, list/show, restart, same-key recreation; record exact failure sizes, failure modes, latency. (2) Test whether --metadata=@file is faithful on create with read-back: if so, switching BdClient lifts the ceiling and may remove the need for git-backed bodies entirely. Hazard: @file is broken for --event-payload, storing the literal '@file' and exiting 0 (client.py:337-338); _assert_metadata (client.py:404) read-back-verifies metadata so a break would be loud. Gates ADR 0002 size caps and the ADR 0003 storage mechanism. Does NOT gate ADR 0002 itself.
close_reason: Probe run 2026-09-03 against an isolated /tmp bd workspace. Inline argv (production path): largest payload created AND read-back-verified = 130818 chars; fails at 131329 with OSError Errno 7 'Argument list too long' — the kernel MAX_ARG_STRLEN (32*4096=131072), hit before bd runs. Failure mode is loud, never silent truncation. --metadata @file on create: verified exact at 70KB/200KB/1MB/4MB. --metadata @file on update (root self-ID merge): verified exact at 300KB with sibling keys preserved. Multibyte UTF-8: limit is bytes not chars (60000B ok, 120000B fails). CONCLUSION: phase-0 probe 2 measured a path production never takes; the ceiling is the kernel's, not bd's; switching BdClient to @file lifts it >=30x on both create and merge. Git-object bodies are NOT needed. Recorded in docs/adr/0003.

title: phase-5 LIVE finding: a no-progress gate offers 'approve', which its target node cannot route — the instance stalls permanently
description:
Found by the DRILL-27 live acceptance run (cr-o85.32), instance beads-f3e.
Reproduced deterministically: every subsequent tick returns the same stall.

WHAT HAPPENED. The forced first rejection worked (see cr-o85.32 notes), so the
rework had nothing real to fix and produced a byte-IDENTICAL artifact tree
(68c17b3f for both implement r1 beads-2ua and implement r2 beads-4dg). The §5
NO_PROGRESS breaker fired correctly and opened a human gate at `triage`
(beads-ayz, gate_reason=transition, opening_outcome=done).

`foreman status` named the inbox and rendered the template (the cr-tl3 fix).
A real ssh-keygen ed25519 signature over the canonical payload verified and the
gate closed cleanly: closed_gates=["beads-ayz"]. §9 works end to end.

Then the instance STALLED, permanently:
  {"stalled":"gate route is not a task", ...}   # every tick, forever

ROOT CAUSE. `foreman/gates.py::no_progress_gate` hardcodes
`outcomes=(Outcome.APPROVE, Outcome.ABANDON)` and ignores the target node's own
declared outcomes. Its target here is `triage`, which the shipped
feature-delivery graph declares as
    outcomes = ["rebudget", "abandon"]
with edges `triage --rebudget--> implement` and `triage --abandon--> abandoned`.
So `approve` has NO declared edge from `triage`. Routing falls through to the
graph fallback `[fallback] to = "triage"`, whose target is a GATE node, not a
task — and `foreman/cases.py:393` stalls with "gate route is not a task".

Contrast `exhaustion_gate` immediately above it, which offers
(APPROVE, REBUDGET, ABANDON) — also not the node's declared set, but at least
containing a routable member.

WHY IT MATTERS. The system offered a human an outcome it cannot act on, then
consumed a valid signed approval for it and dead-ended. There is no recovery:
the gate is closed, the outcome is recorded, and every tick re-stalls. A human
who picks the FIRST listed outcome bricks the instance.

FIX DIRECTION (not chosen): derive a gate's offered outcomes from the target
node's declared `outcomes` — as `transition_gate` already does
(`outcomes=node.outcomes or ()`, gates.py:79) — rather than hardcoding a
vocabulary per gate kind. If a breaker genuinely needs a verb the node does not
declare, the validator should refuse the graph at load time instead of letting
the mismatch appear at run time.

Cross-check worth doing: `exhaustion_gate`'s hardcoded APPROVE has the same
shape of problem wherever `on_exhausted` names a node that does not declare it.
close_reason: FIXED and proven live. exhaustion_gate and no_progress_gate now take their outcomes from the TARGET NODE (foreman/gates.py), exactly as transition_gate already did, instead of a vocabulary hardcoded per gate kind. Test: tests/test_foreman_functional.py::test_a_breaker_gate_only_offers_outcomes_its_own_node_can_route asserts the real invariant — every verb a gate offers must route TASK or TERMINAL — over both breaker gates; written RED first and it reproduced the live stall exactly ('triage offers approve, which routes fallback'). The fix exposed a second latent bug: payload_template took outcomes[0] blindly, which was only safe while every gate led with approve; with triage leading with rebudget the rendered template violated §9 (bound_mutation legal IFF outcome is rebudget) and so was no longer signable, breaking the template's own contract. Fixed by skipping rebudget when another verb exists. Proven live on beads-bmr: the ship gate offered ['approve','abandon'], both routable, and approve reached terminal. NOTED: drill 23's own test asserts these gates' region, round and key and never their outcomes — which is why the lab stayed green.

title: phase-5 LIVE finding: nothing tells a real runner the §6 channel protocol — the composed brief is inputs only
description:
Found by the DRILL-27 live acceptance run (cr-o85.32), first attempt, and NOT
findable in the lab: the ShellProfile double always wrote its outcome marker
because the test authored the script that wrote it. A real vendor CLI has no
idea the channel exists.

WHAT HAPPENED. Live instance beads-75j, node `implement`, runner claude-opus-5,
real repo, real bd. The runner did the work correctly — it wrote src/slug.py
and tests/test_slug.py, and `scripts/verify-feature.sh` passed (exit_code 0 in
the recorded evidence). It then exited 0 having:
  - never written $WF_OUTCOME_FILE,
  - never written $WF_EFFECTS_FILE,
  - never committed (the files are still untracked in the worktree).
Outcome graded `fail_code`; halt gate beads-cot opened with
halt_reason=fail_code:implement:beads-cke. evidence.outputs_tree_oid is the
EMPTY tree 4b825dc6.

ROOT CAUSE. The channels are exported into the child env correctly
(supervisor/profile.py:118-131 — ENV_OUTCOME_FILE, ENV_ARTIFACT_DIR,
ENV_EFFECTS_FILE, plus the §7.4 committer identity). What does not exist is any
place that TELLS the runner to use them. foreman/inputs.py::DefaultComposer
composes the brief as `"\n".join(item.text for item in inputs)` plus the
optional FORCED_FIRST_REJECT clause and nothing else, so the argv the profile
builds is `claude -p <the task brief verbatim>`. Nothing in
profiles/claude.py adds a system prompt or preamble. Spec §6:612-619 defines
the three channels and their fail-closed semantics but never assigns the duty
of communicating them.

CONSEQUENCE. As shipped, a real runner cannot reach `done` on a writing node
except by accident. Every live node fails closed. This is a v1 blocker for
§13's "one real small feature, Claude as first foreman".

WHAT WORKED, and it is worth recording: the foreman's fail-closed path is
exactly right. No marker -> fail_code, not a guessed success; the halt gate
opened with a precise halt_reason; `foreman status` surfaced the gate with its
inbox and payload template (the cr-tl3 fix, live).

FIX OPTIONS, not yet chosen:
  a. A runner-protocol preamble owned by the composer (one place, every node,
     derived from the node's own writes/allowed_paths/outcomes so it cannot
     drift from the graph).
  b. A per-profile system-prompt carrying the same, so each vendor phrases it
     in its own idiom.
  c. Declare it the brief author's job and document it — rejected on its face:
     it makes every brief carry harness protocol, and a brief that forgets it
     fails closed with no diagnostic pointing at the omission.

Option (a) is the natural home: the composer already owns brief composition and
already reads the node.
close_reason: FIXED and proven live. foreman/inputs.py::DefaultComposer now prepends the §6 channel contract, rendered per node from its OWN permissions and declared outcomes (constants.py RUNNER_PROTOCOL + the write/no-write step). implement gets 'git add and git commit ... <one of: done, no_diff, fail_plan>'; review gets 'Do NOT write to the repository ... <one of: accept, reject>'. Test: tests/test_foreman_inputs.py::test_compose_tells_the_runner_the_channel_protocol_for_its_own_node, parametrized over both nodes, written RED first. Proven live on instance beads-bmr with the manual preamble REMOVED from brief.md, so the product path is what ran: all four activations wrote both channels and the writing ones committed.

title: phase-5: infra-retry after ANY gate-origin re-mint crashes the tick and strands the instance
description: foreman/cases.py:409-414 builds the INFRA_RETRY mint request via _request() and model_copy(update={'mint_reason', 'predecessor_activation_id'}) — it never clears predecessor_gate_id, which _request() copies verbatim from the closed activation at cases.py:121. Any activation minted from a gate decision (halt approve/rebudget, exhaustion rebudget) carries predecessor_gate_id. When such an activation later closes error_runner, the auto infra-retry request therefore carries BOTH predecessor_activation_id and predecessor_gate_id, and bdio/mint.py:238-244 _assert_reason_matches refuses it: a request with predecessor_gate_id must have mint_reason EDGE. CarrierIntegrityError is caught NOWHERE in workflow_interpreter/foreman/ (cases.py:432 catches only BoundExceededError), so it propagates unhandled out of tick(). The activation stays closed error_runner, so EVERY subsequent tick re-enters the same path: a permanent crash loop with no halt gate, no stalled report, and no human escape at the foreman seam. Secondary: the diagnostic at mint.py:244 is misleading — it interpolates the GATE id with the ACTIVATION predecessor's outcome ('requires its predecessor to have closed edge, but wf-12 closed error_runner').
design: Likely one line: the model_copy(update=...) at cases.py:409 must also set predecessor_gate_id=None. An infra retry re-attempts the same logical activation; its causal predecessor is that activation, not the gate that originally minted it. Needs a ruling on whether gate provenance should instead be preserved by relaxing the mint.py guard — but the guard's stated rationale ('a mislabeled mint would be counted against the wrong 10.2 bound') argues for clearing the field, not relaxing the guard. Confirm no other model_copy over a _request() has the same gap.
acceptance_criteria: A drill-level test drives: dirty-tree refusal -> halt -> approve -> gate-origin re-mint runs -> that activation closes error_runner -> the next tick MINTS an infra retry (no exception), and the node still gets its FULL max_infra_retries because the precondition-refused closes did not count (P14, bdio/bounds.py:360-364). tests/test_foreman_functional.py::test_drill_26_a_real_infra_failure_after_the_dirty_tree_recovery_keeps_the_full_budget is that test and is RED today.
notes: 2026-09-01 FIXED. foreman/cases.py:409 now builds a fresh MintRequest field by field (omitting predecessor_gate_id) instead of _request(...).model_copy(update=...), so _validate_predecessors runs and the carrier invariant is ENFORCED at construction rather than relied upon — Sol's preferred shape over the minimal one-line None. Evidence: the drill-26 P14 test went RED->GREEN with no test edit; mutant B2-M7 (revert the fix) is KILLED by that test, so the fix is load-bearing; mutant B2-M1 (drop the PRECONDITION_REFUSED skip at bdio/bounds.py:360-364) is KILLED by that test, so P14 is now PROVEN — it was unprovable while this defect stood. VERIFIED BY CODE READ: foreman/__main__.py:218-241 builds the status payload with root_id, activations, instance_base_commit, instance_branch_head, stale, and — only if frontier.open_halt is not None — open_halt. It never reports frontier.open_gates, which frontier.py:243 already computes and returns. Meanwhile foreman/tick.py:299 returns TickReport(terminal=...) on the fall-through path with NO opened_gate. CONSEQUENCE: a transition gate (e.g. the ship gate, GateReason.TRANSITION) is announced by exactly ONE TickReport.opened_gate, at the tick that opens it, and never again by any surface. A human who misses that single report — or whose foreman crashed in the 6a window before it was emitted (cr-hmm) — has no CLI signal that a gate is waiting for a signed decision. The instance is not stuck in any state the code considers wrong; it is simply invisible. NOT 6a-specific: the crash only guarantees the report is missed. This is the general case. SUGGESTED FIX: include frontier.open_gates in the status payload the same way open_halt is included, with the inbox path and payload template per gate. NOTE the interaction with cr-hmm: if status listed open transition gates, the delayed-backfill gap would be audit-only, which is what the round-2 brief provisionally assumed it already was.
acceptance_criteria: foreman status reports every open gate, not only halt gates, with enough detail for a human to submit a signed payload; a drill asserts a transition gate is discoverable on a tick AFTER the one that opened it.
notes:
REVERSED (2026-09-02, same session). The P1 escalation above was WRONG on two
counts, and the reversal is evidence-based.

1. There is NO notification requirement in the spec. The word "notification"
   occurs exactly ONCE in docs/specs/workflow-interpreter.md, at :863, and it
   is a WINDOW MARKER naming where the 6a crash lands — not a contract. The
   actual 6a requirement is the clause's own predicate: "re-tick converges, no
   duplicate gate (same key), no duplicate edge."
2. Spec:729 is explicit: **"Gates wait indefinitely in v1."** Waiting is the
   designed state, not a stall.

And the gate is NOT invisible. `bdio/gates.py:221-224` creates it as a durable
bd bead with a human-readable title (`_TITLE_GATE.format(gate_node, seq)`) and
logs `wf.gate.opened`. It is discoverable by `bd list --status=open` — the
issue tracker IS this system's durable store, and is exactly where a human is
expected to find waiting work. `foreman status` omitting open transition gates
is a UX nicety, which is what this bead is now scoped to.

Spec 6a is moreover ALREADY ASSERTED END TO END at
tests/test_foreman_e2e.py:292-359: converges (`opened_gate is None`, :314), no
duplicate gate (`len(lab.beads("gate")) == 1`, :340), no duplicate edge
(`events_backfilled == 2` then unchanged on re-tick, :356-359). The missed
event is backfilled exactly once at the next routing tick.

Sol's BLOCKER 1 does not survive the spec text. Fable's ruling stands. My own
"silent stall" escalation was an overclaim of the same species S1 exists to
catch, committed while adjudicating S1. Recorded here deliberately.

Re-scoped P1 -> P3, defect -> enhancement: make `foreman status` report
`frontier.open_gates` (frontier.py:243 already computes it) so a waiting
transition gate is visible without a `bd list`.
close_reason: FIXED. foreman/__main__.py status now reports open_gates — every OPEN gate, halt and transition alike — each with gate_id, node, reason, its inbox path and its unsigned payload template. open_halt kept unchanged for existing consumers. Test: tests/test_foreman_main.py::test_status_reports_an_open_transition_gate_with_its_inbox_and_template. Mutation-proven: filtering the new list back to HALT gates only (the exact pre-fix defect) turns the test RED. Motivation is operational, not the earlier 'silent stall' reasoning: status is the ONLY command that renders a gate inbox and payload template, and the shipped feature-delivery graph's ship and triage gates are both gate_type=human TRANSITION gates — so the live DRILL-27 acceptance (cr-o85.32) could not be driven by a human without this.

title: phase-5: a transition event missed by a 6a-window crash is NOT redelivered on re-tick — it waits for the next routing decision
description: Found by S1 batch 7 (2026-09-02) when injection point 6a was finally injected where the spec says: between gate persistence and its first notification. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: Foreman.tick() calls _backfill ONLY in the abandoned_halt branch (tick.py:272) and the head-routing branch (tick.py:277). Not in the dead_end branch, not in the empty/entry-mint branch, and not on the gate-intake path, which returns earlier. CONSEQUENCE: after a crash in the 6a window the gate bead has landed but its transition event has not, and the immediate re-tick backfills NOTHING (events_backfilled == 0) because the landed gate already consumes its source activation, so no routing decision remains to trigger the sweep. The event stays durably absent — never duplicated — until the next tick that takes ANY routing decision; in the drill that is the tick routing the closed ship gate to terminal, which then writes both outstanding events at once (events_backfilled == 2). An instance parked at an open gate awaiting a human keeps the event missing for that entire period. SPEC GAP: docs/specs/workflow-interpreter.md:861-863 says 'crash between gate-open and first notification ... => re-tick converges', which reads as immediate. It does not converge on re-tick. NOT yet classified as a correctness defect: events are a derived audit projection (bdio/bounds.py ceiling_count docstring excludes them) and nothing in routing reads them, so this looks like an audit-completeness and spec-wording gap rather than a control-flow bug. NEEDS A RULING: is delayed backfill the intended contract for anything downstream that watches transition events to know a transition occurred? The test now asserts the ACTUAL behaviour (0, 0, then 2) rather than the row's implied shape.
acceptance_criteria: Either the spec text is corrected to describe delayed backfill, or _backfill is called on the paths that currently skip it and the drill asserts immediate convergence.
notes:
SUPERSEDED IN SUBSTANCE by the cr-tl3 adjudication (round-2 sign-off).

This bead was filed as "6a leaves a transition event unbackfilled". That half is
NOT a defect: `_backfill` runs on the next edge-taking tick (tick.py:277), so
the event is reconstructed once the gate's payload is submitted. Spec §3.3:475
defines events as an idempotently reconstructible audit projection, which this
satisfies. The gap is audit latency bounded by the gate's lifetime.

The REAL defect the 6a analysis exposed is notification, not backfill, and it
lives on cr-tl3 (raised to P1). Close this one in favour of cr-tl3 unless the
latency itself is judged unacceptable.

Earlier correction retained: "nothing in routing reads events" is FALSE —
frontier.py:141-161 reads TERMINAL events for `terminal` and consumption.
close_reason: Not a defect. The 6a event gap is audit latency bounded by the gate's lifetime, and spec 3.3:475 defines events as an idempotently reconstructible audit projection. Already asserted end to end at tests/test_foreman_e2e.py:292-359, including the exactly-once backfill at the next routing tick. See cr-tl3 for the reversal record.

title: phase-5: worktree HEAD does not follow worktree_add's commit argument — mutant survives, mechanism unresolved
description: Found while mutation-grading cr-o85.33.12 (2026-09-02). Mutating supervisor/gitio.py worktree_add to check out f'{commit}^' instead of commit SURVIVES the head-clause test's assertion 'lab.git.head_commit(cwd=worktree) == artifact.commit_oid'. Probed, not inferred: (1) worktree_add is called exactly once with the correct intended commit (instrumented print); (2) under the mutant the git command SUCCEEDS, rc=0, stderr 'Preparing worktree (resetting branch wf/wf-1; was at abfc8d1)' — so the branch reset provably lands; (3) yet head_commit(cwd=worktree) still reads artifact.commit_oid at the assertion point. Something re-establishes the worktree HEAD after the reset, and it is not review's own run (writes=false, no commit). CONSEQUENCE: the head clause's assertion 3 ('the reviewer's worktree is created at that commit') is ASSERTED BUT NOT MUTATION-PROVEN — no mutant found that discriminates it. It may be implied by assertion 1 (the branch advance) given -B semantics, in which case it is a redundant guard rather than a defect; that is the hypothesis to test. NOT a known product defect; an unexplained observation that should be explained before anyone relies on assertion 3.
acceptance_criteria: Either a mutant that kills assertion 3 (making it mutation-proven), or a written explanation of why the worktree HEAD cannot diverge from the instance branch here, recorded in learnings.md.

description: resolve.py:131-138 collects roles ONLY from runners starting with 'profile:', so a node declaring e.g. runner='script:checks/route.sh' is skipped by the unknown-roles refusal AND by _resolved_config's role binding (resolve.py:171). title: phase-5: a §8.1 continuation's §5.4 precondition resets away the steered runner's uncommitted work (R1 consequence, probed)
description:
Reachable for the first time now that R1 makes a steer continuation dispatchable through Supervisor.run. Probed on a real worktree, real steer, real continuation:

  before steer, worktree holds: ['half-done.txt', 'scripts', 'src']
  continuation lifecycle: exit-recorded
  after continuation, worktree holds: ['scripts', 'src']
  reset_applied: True
  prereset refs: ['refs/wf/wf-1/prereset/wf-3']

Supervisor.run runs the same 5.4 precondition for a continuation as for any other activation. In worktree mode Workspace._plan takes snapshot=None, so every dirty path is 'resettable' with no attribution test, and _apply resets to intended_base_commit. The work is NOT lost — _pin_pre_reset commits and pins the whole dirty state first, under the CONTINUATION's activation id (refs/wf/<root>/prereset/<continuation>) — but the continuation's runner starts from a clean tree, not from where the steered runner left off.

Whether that is right is a spec question, not a defect: 8.1 says a steer continues a SESSION, and 5.4 says every dispatch proves a clean tree against its intended base. A continuation resuming a vendor session whose working tree has been reset under it is at least surprising. Phase 5 should settle it: either 8.1 continuations skip the reset (and 5.4 gains an exception with a reason), or the reset stays and 8.1 documents that a steer costs the uncommitted tree, recoverably. Probe: scratchpad/probes/phase4-cli-probes.md-adjacent scratch script probe_continuation_reset2.py. Nothing in phase 4 routes on either answer.
notes: USER RULING 2026-08-26: keep OPEN, deal with later. Phase 5 builds on the reset-stands behaviour (run.py comment stands); nothing in phase 5 routes on this.

title: phase-5: run.jsonl is runner-writable by construction, and scan_log reads a session id and usage back out of it (R7)
description: launch.py::_child dup2s <activation>/run.jsonl onto the child's fd 1 and fd 2, so the runner holds a write handle to a wrapper-dir file outside channels/ and outside every sandbox grant. That is by design — it is the runner's own stream — but BaseProfile.scan_log reads the session id and the token counts back out of it (_base.py:494-516), so a runner can name its own session and its own usage. Nothing routes on either in phase 4 (6 makes usage: unknown legal, max_wall is the ceiling that holds). Recorded at paths.CHANNELS_DIR as a gotcha. Phase 5 must not start routing on scan_log output — a token ceiling or a resume hint derived from it is derived from runner input.

description: gitio.HARDENING pins core.hooksPath / core.pager / core.fsmonitor and ENV_HARDENING drops both ambient config files. filter.<name>.clean cannot be pinned generically (the driver name comes from the repository's own .gitattributes) and diff.external, core.sshCommand, credential.helper, init.templateDir, core.alternateRefsCommand, uploadpack.packObjectsHook are unpinned. What is left is claude's cooperative Bash residual on writes=true (0.3), which a -c pin does not close either — a granted shell can edit .gitattributes and unset the wrapper's env. Revisit if a fourth vendor arrives with a directory grant and no .git protection, or if GitSubcommand ever gains a member that recurses into a submodule (the nested-repo .git residual from P2.3).

title: phase-5: codex cannot pre-assign a session id, against §5.2 (probe finding 6)
description:
thread_id arrives in the first --json line and is settable nowhere, so CodexProfile.prepare returns '' and the id is discovered from output. §5.2 says never discovered. Recorded as a vendor deviation.

PHASE-4 r2 CONSEQUENCE (R1): a codex activation is now UNSTEERABLE for its whole run. Steerer.steer refuses with ContinuationRefused before writing the intent and before the kill whenever the resolved session id is empty, and for codex it is empty from dispatch until the exit envelope is collected — nothing writes the discovered thread id back onto the recorded handle mid-run. That is deliberately fail-closed (the old order killed the child first and only then found out build_resume_command could not name a session), but it means tier-2 steering does not work for this vendor at all.

The obvious fix — scan the live run.jsonl for thread.started and record it — collides with R7/cr-o85.17: run.jsonl is dup2'd onto the child's fd 1 and fd 2, so its contents are runner input. Phase 5 has to decide whether a resume TARGET may come from there, and if so what makes the first thread.started line trustworthy (first-line-wins, recorded once at first observation, never re-read). Test: tests/test_profiles_steer.py::test_steering_a_runner_with_no_resumable_session_refuses_before_the_kill.

title: bdio: package modules reach into BdClient._merge_metadata / _create_bead / _close_bead
description: roots.py, gates.py, canary.py, finalize.py, api.py, supervision.py and transitions.py all call the transport's package-private write methods. That IS the established convention — the methods are private to keep them off the PUBLIC surface (§0.1), not off sibling modules — and ruff's default rule set has no SLF001, so nothing flags it. Worth a decision rather than a drift: either name the convention in the package docstring or give the transport an explicit package-internal facade. Ruled Debt-OK by both r3 critics.

title: supervisor: ExitObserver reaches PinOutcome.REFUSED indirectly
description: At a normal exit ExitObserver calls Workspace.pin_artifact with quarantine=False, so an unattributable in-repo commit yields identity=None and §7 grades fail_code via 'done claim produced no commit; that is no_diff (§7.4)'. Safe — the commit is still HEAD so nothing is unreachable, and the refusal is logged at error — but the outcome is reached by an unrelated clause rather than by naming the refusal, and the reason string pin_artifact computed never reaches the evidence. Ruled Debt-OK by both r3 critics.

title: supervisor: Monitor.watch holds on INDETERMINATE with no ceiling
description: Monitor.watch returns only on a TERMINAL verdict, and INDETERMINATE (liveness unanswerable, or a max_wall termination that could not prove death) is deliberately non-terminal — holding position is the point (§5.6: absence of evidence is not evidence of death). But there is no ceiling on how long it holds, so a permanently unreadable /proc wedges a resident supervisor until a human ends it. Needs a policy decision first: what a wrapper should DO after N minutes of unanswerable liveness, given that recording an exit is exactly what must not happen. Ruled Debt-OK by both r3 critics.

title: bdio: recorded_precondition raises a raw ValidationError on an out-of-band trio
description: ActivationMetadata.pre_attempt_commit/reset_verified_commit are unvalidated str|None, so a bd row whose §3.2 trio was written out-of-band (hand-edit, older tool, direct bd update) makes bdio.supervision.recorded_precondition construct a PreconditionRecord that fails the CommitOid pattern. title: Command: sync -> rescan -> diff -> re-analyse -> recommend
description:
Turn the harness-evaluate skill (or a new command) into a single invocation that chains the whole reference-harness loop:

1. Sync reference_harnesses submodule pins to upstream HEAD.
2. Re-run scan.py to refresh catalogs/, then export_csv.py to refresh inventory/.
3. Diff against the previous catalogs: which skills are new, changed, or gone.
4. For changed/new skills only, run the consolidation analysis (see docs/plans/skill-consolidation-plan.md and the casebook) against the current adopted roster.
5. Output a recommendation per affected skill: ADD (new capability we lack), UPDATE (upstream now better than our adopted version), DOWNGRADE/REPLACE (our pick is no longer the best), or NO-CHANGE.
6. Append the new round to the casebook; never rewrite prior rounds.

Prerequisite: the casebook append-only log must exist first (harness_lifecycle/casebook/). Do not build until the casebook schema has settled through at least one manual round.
